faq.a: A diode lets current flow in only one direction, like a one-way valve in a pipe. It protects circuits from batteries put in backwards and helps turn AC into DC.

faq.q: Which way does current flow through a diode?
faq.a: From the anode to the cathode. The cathode end is marked with a stripe on the diode and a bar on the circuit symbol, which looks like an arrow pointing the way current can go.
asks: What does the stripe on a diode mean?

faq.q: Why does a diode block current backwards?
faq.a: Inside is a junction between two kinds of treated silicon. Backwards, the battery pulls charges away from the junction, widening an empty zone that current cannot cross.
asks: What happens in a reversed diode?

faq.q: How do diodes turn AC into DC?
faq.a: Alternating current flips back and forth. Diodes let only the forward pushes through, giving a bumpy one-way current, and a capacitor smooths the bumps into steady direct current.
Yes. An LED is a diode made of materials that give off light when current flows the forward way. Like any diode, it stays dark if connected backwards.
asks: Why is it called a light-emitting diode?

facts: A silicon diode typically drops about 0.6 to 0.7 volts when it conducts.
The stripe printed on a diode marks its cathode end.

quiz.why: Reversed, the diode's barrier widens and blocks the current, so almost nothing flows.

wrong.1: A diode cannot add push; reversed, it blocks.
